name: Vale Apple
description: Red as a smith's door. The only apple trees in Wickmere grow in Tamwick's orchards, and everyone will tell you so.

name: Watercress
description: Peppery cress from the Larkbourne, the chalk stream that never clouds.

name: Hawthorn Berry
description: Haws from the hedgerows. Vale grandmothers boil them for the heart; the hedge-wights were buried under the same bushes.

name: Yew Berry
description: Bright berries from the barrow yews. The flesh is sweet and the seed is a small death; the Vale plants yews on graves so the dead have something to be careful of.

name: Marsh Marigold
description: Gold cups picked from a punt in the Sedgemire channels. Reedfolk float them at water-burials.

name: Sundew
description: A sticky red marsh plant that eats flies. Patient, like everything in the marsh.

name: Eel Liver
description: The liver of a lake-eel from the Gullhithe drying racks. Oily, dark, and better than it sounds.

name: Indigo Root
description: The root of the marsh indigo. Chewed raw it stains the tongue blue for a week, which in Isseva is a way of saying you meant it.

name: Bracket Fungus
description: A shelf of tough fungus from a black-ash trunk. The Woodfolk dry it for tinder and for a tea they do not offer to strangers.

name: Foxglove
description: Purple bells from the Briarwold clearings. Beautiful, and the Woodfolk's quiet answer to poachers.

name: Hanging Moss
description: Grey-green moss that hangs from the giant oaks like old beards. It grows only where nothing has been said aloud for a while.

name: Briar Thorn
description: A thorn as long as a finger, cut from the Thornmarch. The Briar was grown on purpose; the thorn remembers the purpose better than anyone.

name: Heather Honey
description: Dark honey from the Skerrow moor, thick enough to stand a spoon in. Clan hosts give it to guests; guests who steal it are remembered.

name: Map Lichen
description: Scraped from limestone pavement. It grows a finger's width in a hundred years, so the oldest patches are older than the Toll.

name: Cottongrass
description: White tufts from the high bog. Clan runners chew it on the chain bridges; it steadies the wind in the chest.

name: Ash Poppy Petal
description: A petal from one of Cinderlea's red poppies. There is one to every square mile, and the pilgrims know each of them by name.

name: Grey Grass Seed
description: Seed of the grey grass that grows over the Builders' city. It sprouts grey, seeds grey, and makes no sound in the wind.

name: Bell-Mould
description: Green-blue mould that grows only on old bell-bronze. The Tolling Order scrapes it from the chapter-house bell and calls it the bell's beard.
